scope: Review only Leadership additions made by the July 2026 parent-category backfill. Preserve pre-existing Leadership tags, every Teamwork tag, and all other categories. Retain both categories when leading people and collaboration are substantive. This is not a complete reclassification of the archive.
method: GPT-6 Luna full-text triage with the CMS category definitions, followed by source review and editorial decisions. The triage is advisory: decisions below override it where the article substantively develops direction-setting, delegation, mentoring, or developmental feedback. Evidence excerpts are checked against the original article text. No model-generated output is applied without an explicit retained/removed decision.

criteria.Leadership: Apply when the article substantially explains leading or managing people and teams: setting direction and priorities, aligning people around a goal, delegating authority and responsibility, coaching and developing others, giving performance feedback, resolving people conflicts, or taking responsibility for a team's outcomes. Leadership can come from a manager, a technical lead, or an individual contributor influencing others; a formal title is not required. Collaboration, code review, handoffs, shared workflows, or team productivity alone do not establish Leadership unless the work of guiding, managing, or developing people is itself a strongly developed subject. The author's role and historical parent tags are not evidence. Evaluate independently of Teamwork; use both only when each subject is substantively developed.
criteria.Teamwork: Apply when the article substantially explains how people work together: collaboration among peers or across functions, communication, handoffs, sharing knowledge, coordinating dependent work, joint problem-solving, and shared review or delivery practices. The focus is the team's interactions and collective execution. Leading or managing people, setting their direction, delegation, or developing reports does not by itself establish Teamwork; the collaboration itself must receive substantive attention. A team setting, a manager's presence, or a tool used by a team is insufficient. Evaluate independently of Leadership. Both categories may apply when collaboration and leading people are each strongly developed subjects.
